subject: Architecture
title: Light Pollution: Erasing the Stars
description: A 60-second lesson on Light Pollution: Erasing the Stars.

hook.text: 80% of Americans can no longer see the Milky Way from where they live. Buildings and streetlights erased it.

buildup.text: Upward-facing lights on buildings scatter off atmosphere particles — creating a dome of artificial glow over cities.

discovery.text: Light pollution disrupts animal behavior — sea turtles follow city lights instead of moonlit oceans.

twist.text: Blue-white LED streetlights are worse than old sodium lights — they scatter more broadly across the sky.

climax.text: Dark sky preserves and shielded lighting designs are slowly bringing stars back to the edges of cities.

punchline.text: We lit up our cities and blacked out the universe.

quiz.question: Why are LED streetlights worse for light pollution than older sodium lights?
options: They use more electricity and stay on longer
Blue-white light scatters more broadly across the sky
They are mounted higher on taller poles

details.summary: Artificial light from buildings, signs, and streetlights has erased the night sky for 80% of humanity. Architectural lighting design rarely considers its impact beyond the property line, creating a cumulative glow that disrupts wildlife, wastes energy, and disconnects humans from the cosmos.
details.whyItMatters: Light pollution is architecture's most invisible failure. Every upward-facing fixture and over-lit facade contributes to a global problem that harms ecosystems, human health, and our fundamental connection to the night sky.
takeaways: 80% of humanity lives under light-polluted skies
Buildings and streetlights create a cumulative urban glow
Light pollution disrupts wildlife, wastes energy, and harms health

faq.question: How does building design contribute to light pollution?
faq.answer: Upward-facing spotlights, unshielded fixtures, excessive facade illumination, and interior light spilling through glass curtain walls all send light into the sky. Many buildings are dramatically over-lit relative to need.

faq.question: Can light pollution be fixed?
faq.answer: Yes. Dark-sky-compliant fixtures that direct light downward, warm-toned LEDs instead of blue-white, dimming after midnight, and architectural lighting codes can dramatically reduce sky glow. Tucson, Arizona, and Flagstaff have implemented such measures while maintaining safe, attractive nightscapes.
